headline: 愛丁堡藝穗喜劇周報
context: 愛丁堡藝穗節上，愛爾蘭喜劇演員 Marty Gleeson 帶來風格獨特的個人秀《Dog Ear》。同一週，杜倫市（Durham）的新美術館也開幕，展出多位藝術家的光影作品。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Pleasance Courtyard, Edinburgh Even one of her own bugs takes the mic as the wild card comedian delivers these disconnected bits There’s an excellent joke about art school in Marty Gleeson’s show, but even without it, we might guess that the Irish comic comes from an art school background. In Dog Ear, convention is for the birds, with one leftfield idea following the next in a disorienting array. A visit to the future accompanied by fluttering beats on the bodhrán? A standup set performed by one of the thousands of bugs on Gleeson’s body? A funeral for her 187-year-old alter ego, at which she must solemnly shake the hand of every single audience member? Throughout her fringe debut, Gleeson delights in ensuring we’ve never the slightest idea what’s about to happen next. That makes it an offbeat delight to encounter, and at its best, this Limerick exile’s material is captivatingly unexpected. Even before its droll punchline, her routine about asking Santa, increasingly ardently, for a “big juicy booty” is quite the gambit. Another, extending the closing credits of a news bulletin ad absurdum, is similarly strange – and, like much of her material, tests the limits of how long something uneasy can happen before a punchline arrives to redeem it. 愛丁堡藝穗：愛爾蘭喜劇演員的怪奇個人秀

愛丁堡藝穗節上，愛爾蘭喜劇演員 Marty Gleeson 帶來個人秀《Dog Ear》，內容天馬行空，從未來旅行到向聖誕老公公許願都有。

同一週，杜倫市的新美術館「The Light」開幕，展出包含奧拉佛．艾利亞森（Olafur Eliasson）在內多位藝術家的光影作品。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian，2026 年 8 月 28 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
threads_text:
愛丁堡藝穗節上，愛爾蘭喜劇演員 Marty Gleeson 帶來個人秀《Dog Ear》，內容天馬行空，從未來旅行到向聖誕老公公許願都有，評論形容她總能讓觀眾完全猜不到下一秒會發生什麼。

同一週，杜倫市的新美術館「The Light」開幕，展出包含奧拉佛．艾利亞森（Olafur Eliasson）在內多位藝術家的光影作品，展覽名稱取自 1913 年一齣俄國未來主義舞台劇。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 8 月 28 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 愛丁堡藝穗節上，有一齣個人秀特別怪。愛爾蘭喜劇演員 Marty Gleeson 的《Dog Ear》，內容天馬行空——一下子是未來旅行，一下子又是向聖誕老公公許願，讓人完全猜不到下一秒會發生什麼。同一週，杜倫市開了一間新美術館，展出好幾位藝術家的光影作品，其中包括知名藝術家奧拉佛．艾利亞森。展覽的名字，借用了一齣一百多年前俄國舞台劇的名字。
